title: Rotated Digits
approach: Validate digits and track a changed digit
statement: Count integers from 1 through n whose digits are valid under a 180-degree rotation and whose rotated value differs.
explanation: Reject any number containing 3, 4, or 7; count it only if it contains at least one of 2, 5, 6, or 9.

title: Rotate String
statement: Return true if goal can be obtained by rotating s any number of positions.
explanation: Strings of equal length are rotations exactly when goal is a substring of s concatenated with itself.

title: Unique Morse Code Words
statement: Return the number of distinct Morse encodings among the given lowercase words.
explanation: Translate each character through the Morse table and store each full encoding in a set.

title: Number of Lines To Write String
statement: Given each lowercase letter’s width, return the number of lines needed and the width of the last line when each line holds at most 100 units.
explanation: Append each character to the current line if it fits; otherwise start a new line with that character.

title: Subdomain Visit Count
approach: Accumulate counts for every suffix domain
statement: Given count-and-domain entries, return visit totals for each domain and each of its subdomains.
explanation: Split each domain into labels and add its count to the full domain and every suffix.

title: Most Common Word
approach: Normalize words and count allowed tokens
statement: Return the most frequent word in a paragraph that is not in the banned list, ignoring case and punctuation.
explanation: Extract alphabetic tokens in lowercase, skip banned words, and select the highest-frequency token.
example: paragraph="Bob hit a ball, the hit BALL flew far after it was hit.", banned=["hit"] -> "ball"

title: Shortest Distance to a Character
statement: For each character position, return its distance to the nearest occurrence of c.
explanation: Sweep left-to-right for the previous occurrence and right-to-left for the next occurrence, keeping the smaller distance.

title: Goat Latin
statement: Convert each word to Goat Latin: consonant-leading words move the first letter to the end, then append ma and an increasing run of a characters.
explanation: Split on spaces, apply the vowel/consonant rule, and append ma plus one more a for each word position.
example: sentence="I speak Goat Latin" -> "Imaa peaksmaaa oatGmaaaa atinLmaaaaa"

title: Positions of Large Groups
statement: Return inclusive start and end indices of every run of at least three identical adjacent characters.
explanation: Scan maximal runs and record the bounds when their length is at least three.

title: Flipping an Image
statement: Reverse each binary matrix row and invert every bit.
explanation: For each row, swap symmetric positions while XOR-inverting the values, or reverse then invert.
